1.0.3: Add catch and log errors while processing individual rows
2.0.0: Breaking change: Improve security by restricting all SQL queries to SELECT/WITH statements only and implementing parameterized queries.
2.0.1: Reduced icon size for better performance.
2.0.2: UpdatedRow: declare detectOnStop in properties.schema.properties so the inspector input reaches the trigger.
2.0.3: Added output examples to component schemas.
2.1.0: Added test() (Flow Test Mode) to all triggers: NewRow, UpdatedRow, DeletedRow, WatchRows.
3.0.0: Breaking change: replaced the unmaintained mysql driver with mysql2. Adds support for the caching_sha2_password authentication (the default on MySQL 8.x; MySQL 8.4 disables mysql_native_password by default and MySQL 9 removes it).

Added optional SSL/TLS settings to the connection form: Use SSL (encrypted, server certificate not verified) and CA Certificate (encrypted, server certificate verified against the CA). Existing accounts without these fields connect without SSL as before.

All components and the connection check now share one set of connection options. Query now returns DATE/DATETIME/TIMESTAMP values as strings as returned by MySQL (e.g. '2024-05-01 10:00:00') instead of ISO dates converted to UTC, and BIGINT values outside the safe integer range as strings instead of rounded numbers, the same way the triggers already did.

Value differences of the new driver: ZEROFILL integer columns are returned as numbers (leading zeros are lost; the old driver returned a string). DECIMAL values are always returned as numbers; in triggers, DECIMAL values outside the safe integer range were strings before and are now rounded numbers. JSON columns are still returned as strings, BIT columns as binary data, TIME as strings.
An invalid Port value (not a number) is now rejected with a clear error.
Triggers: the Storage input is a text field with suggestions, so a data store ID can be entered when the list cannot be loaded.
